What this page practises

  • I can explain the Doppler effect in terms of wavefronts.
  • I can use fo = fs (v ÷ (v ± vs)) to find fo or vs.
  • I can state whether fo is higher or lower, and justify it.
  • I can state that the Doppler effect also shifts light.

Warm-up

Say it the exam way

A sound source moves towards an observer. The wavefronts in front of it are . The observer hears a frequency.

The source then moves away. The wavefronts behind it are , so wavefronts reach the observer each second. The frequency heard is . The frequency of the source itself .

This is the effect. It causes shifts in the wavelengths of sound and of light. For a source moving towards the observer, the bottom of the fraction is .

Answers

Say it the exam way

(1) closer together · (2) higher · (3) further apart · (4) fewer · (5) lower · (6) does not change · (7) Doppler · (8) v − vₛ

2026 Paper 1, Question 9: answer E

  • A Not this one. The buzzer's own frequency stays the same, but the frequency heard does not. Think about the wavefronts in front of the buzzer and behind it.
  • B Not this one. The frequency heard does not keep falling. It is higher while the buzzer comes towards the observer and lower while it moves away. It drops as the buzzer passes.
  • C Not this one. Moving away spreads the wavefronts out, so the frequency heard goes down, not up.
  • D Not this one. That is the wrong way round. Coming towards you squashes the wavefronts together, so the first sound is the higher one.
  • E Right. Coming towards the observer, the wavefronts are closer together, so the frequency heard is higher. Moving away, they are further apart, so it is lower.

2016 Section 1, Question 6: answer B

  • A Not this one. This has the fraction upside down and uses v − vs, the sign for a source coming towards you. Use fo = fs × v ÷ (v + vs) for a source moving away.
  • B Right. Away, so use v + vs: fo = 405 × 335 ÷ (335 + 28.0) = 374 Hz.
  • C Not this one. 405 Hz is the horn's own frequency. The car is moving, so the student hears a different frequency.
  • D Not this one. This has the fraction upside down: it multiplies by (v + vs) ÷ v. Use the relationship on the data sheet: fo = fs × v ÷ (v + vs).
  • E Not this one. This uses v − vs, the sign for a source coming towards you. This car is moving away.

2015 Section 1, Question 8: answer E

  • A Not this one. This has the fraction upside down, so the answer is lower than 750 Hz. The ambulance is coming towards the observer, so the frequency heard is higher.
  • B Not this one. This uses v + vs, the sign for a source moving away. This ambulance is coming towards the observer.
  • C Not this one. 750 Hz is the siren's own frequency. The ambulance is moving, so the observer hears a different frequency.
  • D Not this one. This multiplies by (v + vs) ÷ v. Use the relationship on the data sheet: fo = fs × v ÷ (v − vs).
  • E Right. Towards, so use v − vs: fo = 750 × 340 ÷ (340 − 25.0) = 810 Hz.
